# Airstrikes on a market in southwestern Yemen kill at least 30, Houthis say
By The Associated Press

Airstrikes struck a market in southwestern Yemen on Friday, resulting in at least 30 deaths according to Iran-backed Houthi officials. The attack on al-Hadara market in al-Waziyah, Taiz province represents one of the deadliest incidents since recent fighting between Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces resumed. An additional eight people sustained injuries.

Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree stated that "three airstrikes hit the al-Hadara market in al-Waziyah" around 7 a.m. He attributed responsibility to Saudi Arabia, claiming warplanes departed from Khamis Mushait air base and left the province around 8 a.m., though he provided no supporting evidence.

Yemen's Saudi-backed military rejected these claims. Provincial authorities stated "no airstrikes were carried out in the area" and instead blamed the Houthis, referencing what they called "indiscriminate Houthi missile attacks" endangering civilians.

The Associated Press could not independently verify either side's assertions. Saudi Arabia's information ministry has not yet responded to requests for comment.

Footage broadcast by Al-Masirah showed smoke rising from the damaged site, revealing destroyed vehicles, scattered merchandise, and debris throughout the market area. The Houthi health ministry spokesperson, Anees Alsabahi, confirmed casualty figures via social media.

Taiz remains mostly under Houthi control, with the group besieging the provincial capital where Saudi-allied government forces remain positioned.
